findings.text: follow-on: the declared negative control is recorded but never asserted in the landed code — drive() stores each arm's files_after_cold and returns, so a regression that makes arm (c) behave like the default (renamed env var, dropped override) would still exit 0 with a void comparison; the check lives only in the run directory's uncommitted verify-arms-record.sh, so nothing in the repository fails when the harness stops exercising the cache.

follow-on: cache_guard_receipt_text re-parses the CACHE_GUARD_RECEIPT= line that scripts/h200_test_lane/cache_reuse_summary.py:47 (lane_receipt) already owns, and the '-cache' suffix hardcoded at :113 duplicates MARKER_SUFFIX at scripts/h200_test_lane/cache_reuse_summary.py:16; the harness already puts that directory on PYTHONPATH at :72, so the owner is importable and the fork is avoidable, though the owner is fenced to the sibling xla-autotune-cache-off node.

follow-on: COLOURS = {'compile': '#3366cc', ...} reuses a colour the repository has already given to another component — nova/media/ink.py:45 binds #3366cc to DEFAULT_INK.flux_color (confined flux surfaces) — and the figure hand-rolls despine and grid-off rather than importing the repository's one style module or plt.style.use('data-ink') as other benchmark figures do (benchmarks/contour_tree_sweep_placement.py:504), so one hue now names two unrelated things and the colour table is forked beside its owner.

follow-on: the x tick labels are drawn at fontsize=12 while the y tick labels are 14, so a single figure carries two tick-label sizes, against the repository rule that one size is kept throughout a figure (a many-panel figure may drop to 13/11, not mix).

follow-on: the manifest's commits field names 3 of the 6 commits in the landed diff (6fa30f914, 56c7285fb, c9553bd61) and omits 2a5ddb4c4, 44beb1090 and 5fb9a4d83, so a reader comparing the manifest to 3752410851..c9553bd61 cannot account for half the change from the record alone.

item_verdicts.diff: Read commit by commit from 3752410851925e484c79953b2e4e3c3dcb9a6115 to c9553bd61096313e21a346a47a8665753c0d8e32: six commits, 4 files, 1721 insertions, no deletions and no test or product source touched — a 452-line four-arm harness, a research page, a landing fragment and one SVG.
item_verdicts.done_when: The done_when names tests/test_current_book_fragments.py::test_analytic_certificate_moments on one titan GPU through scripts/nova_lane/run.sh --rungs titan in four arms with a fresh node-local root each, and requires the research page to report per-arm compile seconds per program, total compile wall, steady wall over at least three repeats, compile and autotune files, one inspected SVG, and a recommendation from (d) against (c); every one of those is present and the gate that ran is recorded, but the gate log the manifest cites re-derives the record rather than being the measurement log.
item_verdicts.goal: The node's goal is 'Measure what XLA's per-fusion autotuner and its persistent cache cost and buy on the certificate target'; benchmarks/xla_autotune_cache_arms.py:49,276-320 implements the four arms and docs/research/xla-autotune-cache-on-gpfs.html:1-88 reports them, so the landed change does what the goal states.
item_verdicts.manifest: Read manifest.md: status complete, the four arms reported with cold/compile/steady walls and file counts, retry_failures recording six distinct earlier failures with a scaffolding attribution, and the negative control stated in both directions; its commits field names only 3 of the 6 landed commits and its tests field is prose rather than the literal command, which the gate log's own '# command:' line supplies instead.
item_verdicts.write_paths: The node was fenced to benchmarks/xla_autotune_cache_arms.py, docs/research/xla-autotune-cache-on-gpfs.html, docs/figures/forward-solver-route-integrity/xla-autotune-cache, docs/evidence/fragments/forward-solver-route-integrity/xla-autotune-arms.html and docs/figures/forward-solver-route-integrity/xla-autotune-arms; git diff --stat 3752410851925e484c79953b2e4e3c3dcb9a6115 c9553bd61096313e21a346a47a8665753c0d8e32 changes exactly four paths, all inside them.

justifications.durability: The diff adds no assertion that can fail: benchmarks/xla_autotune_cache_arms.py:233-249 returns records and drive() at :317-319 only writes them, so reverting the arm (c) environment override at :84-85 leaves every check green, and the only check that would redden lives in the run directory's uncommitted verify-arms-record.sh.
justifications.evidence: docs/research/xla-autotune-cache-on-gpfs.html:37-58 reports per-arm compile wall, steady walls over three repeats and compile/autotune file counts matching titan-arms-3.json, and gate-arms-record.log ends EXIT=0 with 16 checks, but the cited gate log re-derives the record from durable files rather than being the measurement log and its header names no revision (titan-arms-3.log:6 carries SOURCE_REVISION=6fa30f914).
justifications.fit: benchmarks/xla_autotune_cache_arms.py:390-448 follows the argparse-and-PATH_ROOT idiom of benchmarks/compile_abort_probe.py:1-120, and every name is mechanism-named with no plan label or version, but the figure at :366-371 mixes two tick-label sizes.
justifications.goal_fidelity: benchmarks/xla_autotune_cache_arms.py:276-320 runs the four arms the goal names (default cold, compile cleared with autotune kept, JAX_PERSISTENT_CACHE_ENABLE_XLA_CACHES=none, --xla_gpu_experimental_enable_fusion_autotuner=false) and docs/research/xla-autotune-cache-on-gpfs.html:44-58 states the (d)-against-(c) recommendation the goal asks for.
justifications.reuse: The measurement capability has no owner — searching benchmarks/, scripts/h200_test_lane/ and nova/ by rglob-over-a-cache-root and autotune-subtree classification found no prior compile/autotune split — yet the addition forks two owned pieces: the colour literal at benchmarks/xla_autotune_cache_arms.py:48 against nova/media/ink.py:45 and the receipt parse at :120 against scripts/h200_test_lane/cache_reuse_summary.py:47.
justifications.scope_discipline: git diff --stat 3752410851..c9553bd61 lists only benchmarks/xla_autotune_cache_arms.py, docs/research/xla-autotune-cache-on-gpfs.html, docs/evidence/fragments/forward-solver-route-integrity/xla-autotune-arms.html and docs/figures/forward-solver-route-integrity/xla-autotune-cache/xla-autotune-arms-walls.svg, every one inside the declared write paths, with no test or product source touched.
